result.topic_en: Derivation of the relation 1 − α² − β² − γ² + 2αβγ = 0 among cosines of angles x, y, x+y, its translation into a polynomial relation among side lengths of a quadrilateral, and application to the distances from an arbitrary interior point of a triangle to its vertices.
result.transcription:
Fragmentorum ex Adversariis continuatio. 503
unde fiet $\sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{(1-\beta)(1+\alpha)}{4}}+\sqrt{\frac{(1-\alpha)(1+\beta)}{4}}$
et $\cos\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)}{4}}-\sqrt{\frac{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}{4}}$
At vero ex tertia aequatione $\sin\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{1-\gamma}{2}}$ et $\cos\left(\frac{x+y}{2}\right)=\sqrt{\frac{1+\gamma}{2}}$, unde nascuntur hae duae aequationes
$\sqrt{(1-\beta)(1+\alpha)}+\sqrt{(1-\alpha)(1+\beta)}=\sqrt{2(1-\gamma)}$ et $\sqrt{(1+\alpha)(1+\beta)}-\sqrt{(1-\alpha)(1-\beta)}=\sqrt{2(1+\gamma)}$.
Sumatur prioris quadratum et reperietur $\sqrt{(1-\alpha\alpha)(1-\beta\beta)}=\alpha\beta-\gamma$, hincque denuo sumtis quadratis: $1-\alpha\alpha-\beta\beta-\gamma\gamma+2\alpha\beta\gamma=0$. Hic igitur tantum opus est, ut pro $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ valores substituantur, scilicet
$\alpha=\frac{aa+pp-bb}{2ap},\quad \beta=\frac{dd+pp-cc}{2dp},\quad \gamma=\frac{aa+dd-qq}{2ad};$
quo facto et per denominatorem $4aaddpp$ multiplicando, si termini in ordinem redigantur, erit
$aacc(aa+cc)-aacc(bb+dd+pp+qq)+aabbpp$
$+bbdd(bb+dd)-bbdd(aa+cc+pp+qq)+ccddpp$
$+ppqq(pp+qq)-ppqq(aa+bb+cc+dd)+aaddqq$
$+bbccqq=0.$

Multo brevius autem hoc negotium fieri potest, posito $x+y=z$; erit $\cos z=\cos x\cos y-\sin x\sin y$, ergo $\sin x\sin y=\cos x\cos y-\cos z$ et sumtis quadratis $\sin^2x\sin^2y=\cos^2x\cos^2y-2\cos x\cos y\cos z+\cos^2z$
at est $\sin^2x\sin^2y=1-\cos^2x-\cos^2y+\cos^2x\cos^2y,$
ideoque $1-\cos^2x-\cos^2y+2\cos x\cos y\cos z-\cos^2z=0$, hoc est
$1-\alpha\alpha-\beta\beta-\gamma\gamma+2\alpha\beta\gamma=0;$
reliqua manent, ut ante. Cum igitur sit
$\cos x=\frac{dd+pp-cc}{2dp}=\frac{X}{2dp},\quad \cos y=\frac{aa+pp-bb}{2ap}=\frac{Y}{2ap}$ et $\cos z=\frac{aa+dd-qq}{2ad}=\frac{Z}{2ad},$
hincque fiet $1-\frac{XX}{4ddpp}-\frac{YY}{4aapp}-\frac{ZZ}{4aadd}+\frac{XYZ}{4aaddpp}=0$ et per $4aaddpp$ multiplicando
$4aaddpp-aaXX-ddYY-ppZZ+XYZ=0.$
Sumto nunc (Fig. 66) in triangulo puncto quocunque, ex quo ad singulos trianguli angulos ducantur rectae $x, y, z$, erit
$aaxx(aa+xx)-aaxx(bb+cc+yy+zz)+aabbcc$
$+bbyy(bb+yy)-bbyy(aa+cc+xx+zz)+aayyzz$
$+cczz(cc+zz)-cczz(aa+bb+xx+yy)+bbxxzz$
$+ccxxyy=0$
quae ita disponi potest
$aax^4-xxyy(aa+bb-cc)-aaxx(bb+cc-aa)+aabbcc$
$+bby^4-xxzz(aa+cc-bb)-bbyy(aa+cc-bb)$
$+ccz^4-yyzz(bb+cc-aa)-cczz(aa+bb-cc)=0.$
A. m. T. I. p. 345. 346.

items.quote: Sumto nunc (Fig. 66) in triangulo puncto quocunque, ex quo ad singulos trianguli angulos ducantur rectae $x, y, z$, erit
items.english: Now taking any point in a triangle (Fig. 66), from which straight lines x, y, z are drawn to the individual vertices of the triangle, there will hold [the stated relation among a, b, c, x, y, z].

items.quote: Multo brevius autem hoc negotium fieri potest, posito $x+y=z$
items.english: But this task can be done much more briefly by setting x + y = z.
